parsed.explanation: The quoted sentence invokes an induction whose objects are never defined: the two 'rows'/'arrays' are described only as alternating swept portions, with 'cancellation' pairing 'every common vertical portion' left unexplained (what commonality, between which portions, and why cancellation preserves legality of splits). The text asserts each uncancelled array has at most s column-blocks and total at most (T-d)/2, asserts the subproblem has the same form as the original, and asserts the cuts used are legal splits of the original stick — none of these is established. Since part (i) of the lemma is the sole basis for the all-n upper bound in Section 4, and the argument for it is not written out as a valid proof, the objection identifies a genuine gap that cannot be repaired from elsewhere in the text.
